title: Proof and reasonable certainty of damages
shortTitle: Proof and reasonable certainty of damages
summary: The certainty requirement asks whether evidence supports the existence and amount of the claimed loss sufficiently for an award. It does not always require exact arithmetic or an established business history.
notes:
Fera concerns projected profits of a new business, supported by testimony that the jury could evaluate. The majority and dissent disagreed about the evidence and the weight of uncertainty. The broader materials distinguish uncertainty about whether loss occurred from difficulty measuring a loss known to have occurred.

Identify the assumptions behind projections, the available market or operating evidence, causation, and the standard of review. The fact that a business is new is relevant to proof but should not be used as a substitute for examining the evidence under the applicable rule. Naval Institute supplies an earlier example of a supported counterfactual estimate.
